system_label: ALIBI: lead + integrity-auditor + skeptic with deterministic checks

findings.rationale: A 22 MB file from a patients_full export was written to a hidden /tmp folder about a minute before the non-approved transfer. Its size closely matches the bytes sent.
verifier_notes: an object of matching size was written on this host shortly before a non-approved bulk transfer
findings.skeptic_note: The export file matches the transfer size and the tap corroborates the retrieval.

findings.rationale: The tap recorded 22,158,181 bytes sent from the workstation to 10.20.9.27:8080. That is over the bulk threshold and the destination is not approved. The transfer overlaps console session workstation#91 on the kcole account.
alternative_explanations: The flow record shows how many bytes moved, not what they contained.
Someone else who had the credential could have run the session.
verifier_notes: bulk transfer to a destination not on the approved list, cited via the flow record
findings.skeptic_note: An independent tap witness shows a bulk transfer to a non-approved destination; no benign explanation fits.

findings.rationale: The lines missing on the host all predate the 08:47 rotation. Under the keep-0 policy the rotated segment is archived off-host, which explains the absence.
verifier_notes: a deterministic check supports this observation; it is not an incident allegation
findings.skeptic_note: The rotation with keep 0 explains the missing lines.

findings.rationale: A bulk transfer went to the approved backup destination stor-nas-01.
verifier_notes: a deterministic check supports this observation; it is not an incident allegation
findings.skeptic_note: Transfer to the approved backup destination.

limits: An account identifies a credential, not a person.
Console credentials at the shared station have been found written down before.
Badge records cannot show tailgating; the adm-bsato and aokafor badges were also inside.
attribution.statement: Account used: kcole (console session workstation#91). The human operator is not established.

summary: Supported incidents: (1) Data staging. At 12:18 on the workstation, a 22 MB file from a patients_full export was written to the hidden path /tmp/.font-unix/cache-0a91.bin (F-61b496). (2) Policy-violating transfer. About 22.2 MB went from the workstation to the non-approved destination 10.20.9.27:8080 at 12:19, recorded by the tap (F-fcf5fd). Both happened during console session workstation#91 on the kcole account. Benign: a records backup went to the approved stor-nas-01 (10.20.0.45:873) (F-7f28df). Records access.log lines missing from before 08:47 are explained by rotation (keep 0, archived off-host) (F-2c65e0). There was no log removal and there were no collector gaps. Attribution: the kcole account was used; the human operator is not established.
open_questions: What is 10.20.9.27 and who operates it?
What did the transferred file contain? The flow record shows bytes only.
Who was physically at the shared workstation console at 12:17-12:20? Credentials there have been found written down before.
